hero.title: NVIDIA,
hero.lede: The main supplier of AI compute, read from its filings, product launches and spokesperson statements, not from its CEO. Jensen Huang’s remarks enter here only as context.

short_answer.title: Corporate NVIDIA answers within a day, in writing
short_answer.body: US chip-policy moves, Beijing pressure and smuggling cases each draw a short company statement on the same or next day. US restrictions draw an SEC filing within a week.

short_answer.title: It complies, then redesigns
short_answer.body: Each new export limit has been followed by a chip built to sit just under it. The public fight over the rules is left to its CEO.

purpose.summary: What NVIDIA as a company files, ships, says and funds is in its control, so a persona built from that record can forecast it. It does not forecast Jensen Huang’s personal remarks (his own persona) or whether incidents happen.
use_for: When the US tightens chip exports, how soon does NVIDIA disclose the hit, and does a compliant China chip follow?
When the US eases or tightens chip policy, what does the company say, and how fast?
When Beijing summons or investigates NVIDIA, what does it say?
When a researcher reports a vulnerability, how long until a patch?
Which safety commitments will it sign, and does it change its framework when it does?
dont_use_for: Jensen Huang’s trips, meetings and statements. Those belong to the Jensen Huang persona and appear here as context rows (J…).
Whether an incident or smuggling case happens at all. The persona covers only NVIDIA’s response once it is public.
Product roadmaps and pricing beyond policy-relevant launches.

standing.class_role: Company · the largest supplier of AI accelerators and the CUDA software stack. US-listed (NASDAQ: NVDA).
standing.principal: Its board and shareholders. Its founder-CEO Jensen Huang speaks for it in public most often; his remarks are logged in his own persona.
standing.attribution_rule: A row is NVIDIA’s when it comes from the company: SEC filings, press releases, blog posts, security bulletins, named spokespeople and officers speaking for the company (e.g. its CSO or VP of government affairs). Huang’s personal remarks are context rows from his persona.
standing.veto_players: Commerce/BIS (export licences), the President (deals on top of licences), Congress (statute such as the GAIN AI Act), CAC and SAMR in Beijing (purchases, antitrust), and merger regulators (the FTC, EU and UK, which ended the Arm deal in 2022).
standing.gates_held: GPU supply and allocation, the CUDA software stack, and service and support: diverted products get “no service, support, or updates”.

gates.held_by: Commerce/BIS, with deals set by the President
gates.response: Discloses within a week (K04, K11, K29), then ships a compliant chip (K06, K14, K35)

gates.gate: Purchase permission and antitrust in China
gates.held_by: CAC, SAMR and other Beijing bodies
gates.response: Same-day denial or cooperation statement (K38, K46); guidance assumes zero China revenue (K59)
Abandoned Arm (K01); completed Run:ai after EU clearance (K19)

gates.gate: Service and support for its GPUs
gates.response: Says diverted products get no support (K42); opt-in fleet software can report location (K52)

powers.use: Designs and allocates chips per market, including China-only parts (K06, K07, K35)
powers.limit: What may ship to China is set by BIS licences

powers.use: Ships hardware generations and open-weight Nemotron models (K16, K61)
powers.limit: Its framework says it does not build frontier models

powers.use: Invests in its customers and partners: Intel K48, OpenAI K49, Anthropic K50
powers.limit: The OpenAI deal is a letter of intent, not a definitive agreement

powers.use: Comments on rules and lobbies against them; spend up 388% in H1 2025 (K37)
powers.limit: Most access runs through Huang personally

powers.use: Joins voluntary pacts and sovereign-AI partnerships (K09, K23, K65, K32)
powers.limit: Joins coalitions others convene; the open-weight alliance was led by Huang

powers.use: Publishes a Frontier AI Risk Assessment (K25), revised silently (K39)
powers.limit: Scoped to models it says it does not build; no public changelog

powers.use: SEC filings on export hits; security bulletins and patches
powers.limit: Discloses what securities law and coordinated disclosure require
No suit by NVIDIA in the log

topics.label: China race
topics.neg: China is a threat to contain
topics.pos: China is a peer to engage

incentives: Sell into every market the law allows, including China
Keep developers on CUDA and its open models
Fund its own customers so demand for compute keeps growing

positions.position: Against export controls; welcomes every easing and criticises every tightening
Against hardware kill switches, backdoors and mandated tracking
Releases open-weight models and open safety tooling
Signs voluntary commitments and ships safety tooling, but scopes its framework to frontier models it says it does not build
Follows US rules while planning for zero China revenue

red_lines: Hardware kill switches, backdoors or mandated tracking in its GPUs
Rules that make it serve US buyers first (the GAIN AI Act)
Tiered country caps on chip access (the AI Diffusion Rule)
profile.decision_style: Comply, disclose, redesign. Each new limit draws an SEC filing within a week and, months later, a chip built to sit just under it. Company statements are short and legal (K43); the public argument is left to Huang.

relations.note: Licenses what NVIDIA may ship to China
Summons, purchase guidance and antitrust in China
Its CEO, who carries its access to Trump and Beijing
Opposed on export policy, yet an investee from Nov 2025

voice.summary: Short, legal and declarative. Repeats set phrases across cases: “smuggling is a nonstarter”, “we follow rules the U.S. government sets”.

say_do.say: No hardware tracking, no kill switches
say_do.do: Ships opt-in fleet software that can report a GPU’s location

say_do.say: We follow the rules the US government sets
say_do.do: Lobbying spend rose about sevenfold in 2025, against those rules

say_do.say: Frontier AI models are not under development at NVIDIA

incidents.incident: Lapsus$ breach: credentials and ~1TB of proprietary data taken
incidents.what_changed: Hardened network, engaged responders, notified law enforcement. Public date approximate.

incidents.incident: CVE-2024-0132: Container Toolkit escape (CVSS 9.0), found by Wiz
incidents.what_changed: Fixed in Toolkit 1.16.2; Wiz estimated >35% of cloud environments exposed

incidents.incident: CVE-2025-23359: bypass of the incomplete CVE-2024-0132 patch
GPUHammer: Rowhammer bit-flips on GDDR6 GPUs
incidents.what_changed: Recommends System-Level ECC (mitigation, not a patch)

incidents.incident: Triton Inference Server unauthenticated RCE chain

incidents.what_changed: Same-day denial, then the CSO’s “No Backdoors” post

incidents.incident: DOJ charges ALX Solutions with GPU smuggling
incidents.what_changed: Says diverted products get no support

incidents.what_changed: Bloomberg (unopened) reports NVIDIA cut over half its authorised Asian buyers

rules.name: US restriction → SEC disclosure
rules.when: The US imposes an export restriction that hits NVIDIA
rules.then: NVIDIA files an 8-K within 0-6 days of being told privately; the filing is usually how the public learns, so on a public timeline it lands on day 0
rules.note: Trigger dates are when NVIDIA was told (it is a party to the notice); the public learned from the filing itself.

rules.name: US chip-policy move → same-day statement
rules.when: Washington eases or tightens chip export policy in public
rules.then: NVIDIA issues a statement within a day: praise for easing; criticism or a compliance line for tightening
rules.note: The July 2025 revenue-share report drew a statement (K43) a day before Trump confirmed the deal (C07), so it is not counted.

rules.name: Beijing pressure → denial or cooperation
rules.when: A Chinese regulator summons or investigates NVIDIA
rules.then: NVIDIA answers the same or next day: denies the allegation or says it will cooperate
rules.note: Three bodies, three years. The response never challenges the regulator’s authority.

rules.name: Private vulnerability report → patch
rules.when: A researcher privately reports a critical vulnerability
rules.then: NVIDIA ships a patch and bulletin 25-81 days later, on the day the researcher publishes
rules.note: All three reports came from Wiz, and two arrived two days apart (one wave under P3). One more independent report would make this a pattern.

rules.name: Export limit → compliant China chip
rules.when: A new export limit cuts NVIDIA’s China product
rules.then: A China-specific chip designed to sit just under the limit follows within months
rules.note: Moved here from the Jensen persona (his R6): it is a company act. The H20 date (K14) is month-only, and A800/H800 answer the same trigger, so only two independent waves are computable.

rules.name: Smuggling case public → “nonstarter” statement
rules.when: Prosecutors announce a case involving smuggled NVIDIA chips
rules.then: NVIDIA says the same or next day that smuggling is a nonstarter and diverted chips get no support
rules.note: One build episode (the March 2026 reply K56 is month-only). Both held-out cases fit, so this is the next signal likely to become a pattern.

rules.name: Agent-safety alarm → product, not policy
rules.when: A lab discloses misaligned or rogue AI agents
rules.then: NVIDIA ships safety tooling rather than backing new rules
rules.note: Mirrors Jensen’s R4. Built from held-out rows only, so it still needs a fresh test.

reach.reading: Commerce rescinded the Diffusion Rule 114 days later, after the change of administration. Followed, not caused.
The GAIN AI Act was left out of the defence bill three months later; Huang also lobbied senators in person (J21).
No definitive agreement had been signed by early 2026. The log can’t yet show what the investment moved.

tests.note: No public US chip-policy change between the cutoff and October 2026 drew a logged statement.
Taiwan detention (C52) → statement next day (K62); Lui arrest (C53) → statement next day (K66).
Built from held-out rows (C15, C27), so they cannot also test it.

limits.title: Most rows are reports of statements
limits.body: SEC filings, NVIDIA blog posts and security bulletins were read in the original; spokesperson quotes come from news reports, some through syndicated copies.

limits.title: Left out as unconfirmed
limits.body: A reported ~$12.9bn Hugging Face acquisition (Sept 2026) and a $105bn credit guarantee for an OpenAI data centre (Aug 2026) rest on press summaries, one of them AI-generated. Check both on EDGAR before adding rows.

limits.title: The framework changed without a changelog
limits.body: The Frontier AI Risk Assessment was reissued in August 2025 (K39) at the same URL. What changed is unknown; METR lists only the February version.

limits.title: CEO and company overlap
limits.body: Huang signed the September 2026 accord for NVIDIA and carries most of its access. The attribution rule keeps his remarks in his persona, which makes NVIDIA look quieter on policy than it is.

limits.title: Lobbying is thin
limits.body: Only one lobbying-disclosure row. LDA filings by quarter, and comments on BIS rules, should be pulled directly.

limits.title: No baseline
limits.body: Without a base-rate forecaster, a fit shows consistency, not forecasting skill.
